units.leftText: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
units.rightText: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

units.leftText: to the assembly of God which is at Corinth—those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:
units.rightText: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:

units.leftText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: I always thank my God concerning you for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: that in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and all knowledge—
units.rightText: For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge,

units.leftText: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you—
units.rightText: because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.

units.leftText: so that you come behind in no gift, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
units.rightText: God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.

units.leftText: Now I beg you, brothers, through the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfected together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
units.rightText: I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree together, so that there may be no divisions among you and that you may be united in mind and conviction.
leftNotes: 1:10 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are from Chloe’s household, that there are contentions among you.
units.rightText: My brothers, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.

units.leftText: Now I mean this, that each one of you says, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” and, “I follow Christ.”
units.rightText: What I mean is this: Individuals among you are saying, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”
rightNotes: 1:12 That is, Peter

units.leftText: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?
units.rightText: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized into the name of Paul?

units.leftText: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
units.rightText: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,

units.leftText: so that no one should say that I had baptized you into my own name.
units.rightText: so no one can say that you were baptized into my name.

units.leftText: (I also baptized the household of Stephanas; besides them, I don’t know whether I baptized any other.)
units.rightText: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.

units.leftText: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the Good News—not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ wouldn’t be made void.
units.rightText: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with words of wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.

units.leftText: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
units.rightText: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

units.leftText: For it is written,
units.rightText: For it is written:

units.leftText: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Hasn’t God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
units.rightText: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

units.leftText: For seeing that in the wisdom of God, the world through its wisdom didn’t know God, it was God’s good pleasure through the foolishness of the preaching to save those who believe.
units.rightText: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know Him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.

units.leftText: For Jews ask for signs, Greeks seek after wisdom,
units.rightText: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom,

units.leftText: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Greeks,
units.rightText: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
rightNotes: 1:23 BYZ and TR to Greeks

units.leftText: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God;
units.rightText: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

units.leftText: because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
units.rightText: For the foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength.
rightNotes: 1:25 Literally than men; twice in this verse

units.leftText: For you see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;
units.rightText: Brothers, consider the time of your calling: Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were of noble birth.

units.leftText: but God chose the foolish things of the world that he might put to shame those who are wise. God chose the weak things of the world that he might put to shame the things that are strong.
units.rightText: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.

units.leftText: God chose the lowly things of the world, and the things that are despised, and the things that don’t exist, that he might bring to nothing the things that exist,
units.rightText: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,

units.leftText: that no flesh should boast before God.
units.rightText: so that no one may boast in His presence.

units.leftText: Because of him, you are in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption,
units.rightText: It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.

units.leftText: that, as it is written, “He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”
units.rightText: Therefore, as it is written: “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
rightNotes: 1:31 Jeremiah 9:24|JER 9:24*

units.leftText: When I came to you, brothers, I didn’t come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.
units.rightText: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.

units.leftText: For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.
units.rightText: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.

units.leftText: I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.
units.rightText: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.

units.leftText: My speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
units.rightText: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,

units.leftText: that your faith wouldn’t stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
units.rightText: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.

units.leftText: We speak wisdom, however, among those who are full grown, yet a wisdom not of this world nor of the rulers of this world who are coming to nothing.
units.rightText: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom — but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.

units.leftText: But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that has been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,
units.rightText: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.
rightNotes: 2:7 Or we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery

units.leftText: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.
units.rightText: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

units.leftText: But as it is written,
units.rightText: Rather, as it is written:

units.leftText: But to us, God revealed them through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.
units.rightText: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit.

units.leftText: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man which is in him? Even so, no one knows the things of God except God’s Spirit.
units.rightText: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

units.leftText: But we received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that were freely given to us by God.
units.rightText: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.

units.leftText: We also speak these things, not in words which man’s wisdom teaches but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.
units.rightText: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.
rightNotes: 2:13 Or to spiritual people

units.leftText: Now the natural man doesn’t receive the things of God’s Spirit, for they are foolishness to him; and he can’t know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
units.rightText: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

units.leftText: But he who is spiritual discerns all things, and he himself is to be judged by no one.
units.rightText: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.

units.leftText: “For who has known the mind of the Lord that he should instruct him?” But we have Christ’s mind.
units.rightText: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
rightNotes: 2:16 Isaiah 40:13|ISA 40:13* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Brothers, I couldn’t speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.
units.rightText: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly — as infants in Christ.

units.leftText: I fed you with milk, not with solid food, for you weren’t yet ready. Indeed, you aren’t ready even now,
units.rightText: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,

units.leftText: for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?
units.rightText: for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?

units.leftText: For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you fleshly?
units.rightText: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?

units.leftText: Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed, and each as the Lord gave to him?
units.rightText: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.

units.leftText: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.
units.rightText: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.

units.leftText: So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.
units.rightText: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.

units.leftText: Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
units.rightText: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.
rightNotes: 3:8 Literally are one

units.leftText: For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.
units.rightText: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.

units.leftText: According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.
units.rightText: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.

units.leftText: For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or straw,
units.rightText: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,

units.leftText: each man’s work will be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man’s work is.
units.rightText: his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.

units.leftText: If any man’s work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.
units.rightText: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.

units.leftText: If any man’s work is burned, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but as through fire.
units.rightText: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.

units.leftText: Don’t you know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit lives in you?
units.rightText: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
rightNotes: 3:16 Or among

units.leftText: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which you are.
units.rightText: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.

units.leftText: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool that he may become wise.
units.rightText: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.

units.leftText: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He has taken the wise in their craftiness.”
units.rightText: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”

units.leftText: And again, “The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless.”
units.rightText: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”

units.leftText: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,
units.rightText: Therefore, stop boasting in men. All things are yours,

units.leftText: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come. All are yours,
units.rightText: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future. All of them belong to you,
rightNotes: 3:22 That is, Peter

units.leftText: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.
units.rightText: and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.

units.leftText: So let a man think of us as Christ’s servants and stewards of God’s mysteries.
units.rightText: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

units.leftText: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
units.rightText: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

units.leftText: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by a human court. Yes, I don’t even judge my own self.
units.rightText: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.

units.leftText: For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord.
units.rightText: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.

units.leftText: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.
units.rightText: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.

units.leftText: Now these things, brothers, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you might learn not to think beyond the things which are written, that none of you be puffed up against one another.
units.rightText: Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.

units.leftText: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you didn’t receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
units.rightText: For who makes you so superior? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?

units.leftText: You are already filled. You have already become rich. You have come to reign without us. Yes, and I wish that you did reign, that we also might reign with you!
units.rightText: Already you have all you want. Already you have become rich. Without us, you have become kings. How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!

units.leftText: For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.
units.rightText: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.

units.leftText: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.
units.rightText: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.

units.leftText: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.
units.rightText: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.

units.leftText: We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.
units.rightText: We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;

units.leftText: Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.
units.rightText: when we are slandered, we answer gently. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world.

units.leftText: I don’t write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.
units.rightText: I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.

units.leftText: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.
units.rightText: Even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

units.leftText: I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.
units.rightText: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.

units.leftText: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.
units.rightText: That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.
rightNotes: 4:17 BYZ and TR my way of life in Christ,

units.leftText: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.
units.rightText: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.

units.leftText: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power.
units.rightText: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.

units.leftText: For God’s Kingdom is not in word, but in power.
units.rightText: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

units.leftText: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?
units.rightText: Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit?

units.leftText: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles, that one has his father’s wife.
units.rightText: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is intolerable even among pagans: A man has his father’s wife.

units.leftText: You are arrogant, and didn’t mourn instead, that he who had done this deed might be removed from among you.
units.rightText: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have been stricken with grief and have removed from your fellowship the man who did this?

units.leftText: For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.
units.rightText: Although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did this, just as if I were present.

units.leftText: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together with my spirit with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, along with the power of the Lord Jesus,
rightNotes: 5:4 Or In the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are assembled

units.leftText: you are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.
rightNotes: 5:5 BYZ and TR the Lord Jesus

units.leftText: Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?
units.rightText: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough?

units.leftText: Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place.
units.rightText: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

units.leftText: Therefore let’s keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
units.rightText: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth.

units.leftText: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;
units.rightText: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

units.leftText: yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortionists, or with idolaters, for then you would have to leave the world.
units.rightText: I was not including the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.

units.leftText: But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother who is a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortionist. Don’t even eat with such a person.
units.rightText: But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.

units.leftText: For what do I have to do with also judging those who are outside? Don’t you judge those who are within?
units.rightText: What business of mine is it to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?

units.leftText: But those who are outside, God judges. “Put away the wicked man from among yourselves.”
units.rightText: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked man from among you.”
rightNotes: 5:13 Literally Expel the evil from among you; Deuteronomy 13:5|DEU 13:5*, 17:7, 19:19, 21:21, 22:21, 22:24, and 24:7

units.leftText: Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
units.rightText: If any of you has a grievance against another, how dare he go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints!

units.leftText: Don’t you know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
units.rightText: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?

units.leftText: Don’t you know that we will judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?
units.rightText: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!

units.leftText: If then you have to judge things pertaining to this life, do you set them to judge who are of no account in the assembly?
units.rightText: So if you need to settle everyday matters, do you appoint as judges those of no standing in the church?

units.leftText: I say this to move you to shame. Isn’t there even one wise man among you who would be able to decide between his brothers?
units.rightText: I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?

units.leftText: But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers!
units.rightText: Instead, one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of unbelievers!

units.leftText: Therefore it is already altogether a defect in you that you have lawsuits one with another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
units.rightText: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?

units.leftText: No, but you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and that against your brothers.
units.rightText: Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!
rightNotes: 6:8 Literally do wrong, and this to brothers!

units.leftText: Or don’t you know that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s Kingdom? Don’t be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostitutes, nor homosexuals,
units.rightText: Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts,

units.leftText: nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor extortionists, will inherit God’s Kingdom.
units.rightText: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Some of you were such, but you were washed. You were sanctified. You were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.
units.rightText: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.

units.leftText: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.
units.rightText: “Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.

units.leftText: “Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods,” but God will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
units.rightText: “Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

units.leftText: Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.
units.rightText: By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.

units.leftText: Don’t you know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
units.rightText: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!

units.leftText: Or don’t you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, “The two”, he says, “will become one flesh.”
units.rightText: Or don’t you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”
rightNotes: 6:16 Genesis 2:24|GEN 2:24* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.
units.rightText: But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.

units.leftText: Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
units.rightText: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.

units.leftText: Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,
units.rightText: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

units.leftText: for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.
units.rightText: you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.
rightNotes: 6:20 BYZ and TR include and with your spirit, which belong to God.

units.leftText: Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
units.rightText: Now for the matters you wrote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.
rightNotes: 7:1 Literally It is good for a man not to touch a woman.

units.leftText: But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
units.rightText: But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.

units.leftText: Let the husband give his wife the affection owed her, and likewise also the wife her husband.
units.rightText: The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
leftNotes: 7:3 NU and TR have “what is owed her” instead of “the affection owed her”.

units.leftText: The wife doesn’t have authority over her own body, but the husband does. Likewise also the husband doesn’t have authority over his own body, but the wife does.
units.rightText: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.

units.leftText: Don’t deprive one another, unless it is by consent for a season, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer, and may be together again, that Satan doesn’t tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
units.rightText: Do not deprive each other, except by mutual consent and for a time, so you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control.

units.leftText: But this I say by way of concession, not of commandment.
units.rightText: I say this as a concession, not as a command.

units.leftText: Yet I wish that all men were like me. However, each man has his own gift from God, one of this kind, and another of that kind.
units.rightText: I wish that all men were as I am. But each man has his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.

units.leftText: But I say to the unmarried and to widows, it is good for them if they remain even as I am.
units.rightText: Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.

units.leftText: But if they don’t have self-control, let them marry. For it’s better to marry than to burn with passion.
units.rightText: But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn with passion.

units.leftText: But to the married I command—not I, but the Lord—that the wife not leave her husband
units.rightText: To the married I give this command (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.

units.leftText: (but if she departs, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not leave his wife.
units.rightText: But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.

units.leftText: But to the rest I—not the Lord—say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her.
units.rightText: To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.

units.leftText: The woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is content to live with her, let her not leave her husband.
units.rightText: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.

units.leftText: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
units.rightText: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

units.leftText: Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us in peace.
units.rightText: But if the unbeliever leaves, let him go. The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.
rightNotes: 7:15 SBL, BYZ, and TR us

units.leftText: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
units.rightText: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

units.leftText: Only, as the Lord has distributed to each man, as God has called each, so let him walk. So I command in all the assemblies.
units.rightText: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.

units.leftText: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
units.rightText: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.

units.leftText: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but what matters is keeping God’s commandments.
units.rightText: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.

units.leftText: Let each man stay in that calling in which he was called.
units.rightText: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.

units.leftText: Were you called being a bondservant? Don’t let that bother you, but if you get an opportunity to become free, use it.
units.rightText: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you— but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.

units.leftText: For he who was called in the Lord being a bondservant is the Lord’s free man. Likewise he who was called being free is Christ’s bondservant.
units.rightText: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.

units.leftText: You were bought with a price. Don’t become bondservants of men.
units.rightText: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.

units.leftText: Brothers, let each man, in whatever condition he was called, stay in that condition with God.
units.rightText: Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.

units.leftText: Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.
units.rightText: Now about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.

units.leftText: Therefore I think that because of the distress that is on us, it’s good for a man to remain as he is.
units.rightText: Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.
rightNotes: 7:26 Or impending

units.leftText: Are you bound to a wife? Don’t seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? Don’t seek a wife.
units.rightText: Are you committed to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of commitment? Do not look for a wife.

units.leftText: But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.
units.rightText: But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.

units.leftText: But I say this, brothers: the time is short. From now on, both those who have wives may be as though they had none;
units.rightText: What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they had none;

units.leftText: and those who weep, as though they didn’t weep; and those who rejoice, as though they didn’t rejoice; and those who buy, as though they didn’t possess;
units.rightText: those who weep, as if they did not; those who are joyful, as if they were not; those who make a purchase, as if they had nothing;

units.leftText: and those who use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.
units.rightText: and those who use the things of this world, as if not dependent on them. For this world in its present form is passing away.

units.leftText: But I desire to have you to be free from cares. He who is unmarried is concerned for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
units.rightText: I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the work of the Lord, how he can please the Lord.

units.leftText: but he who is married is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife.
units.rightText: But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this world, how he can please his wife,

units.leftText: There is also a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she who is married cares about the things of the world—how she may please her husband.
units.rightText: and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the work of the Lord, how she can be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about the affairs of this world, how she can please her husband.

units.leftText: This I say for your own benefit, not that I may ensnare you, but for that which is appropriate, and that you may attend to the Lord without distraction.
units.rightText: I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord.

units.leftText: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He doesn’t sin. Let them marry.
units.rightText: However, if someone thinks he is acting inappropriately toward his betrothed, and if she is beyond her youth and they ought to marry, let him do as he wishes; he is not sinning; they should get married.
rightNotes: 7:36 Literally and it ought to be so

units.leftText: But he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no urgency, but has power over his own will, and has determined in his own heart to keep his own virgin, does well.
units.rightText: But the man who is firmly established in his heart and under no constraint, with control over his will and resolve in his heart not to marry the virgin, he will do well.
rightNotes: 7:37 Literally in his heart to keep the virgin or in his heart to keep the betrothed

units.leftText: So then both he who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and he who doesn’t give her in marriage does better.
units.rightText: So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.

units.leftText: A wife is bound by law for as long as her husband lives; but if the husband is dead, she is free to be married to whomever she desires, only in the Lord.
units.rightText: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
rightNotes: 7:39 Literally she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord

units.leftText: But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment, and I think that I also have God’s Spirit.
units.rightText: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.

units.leftText: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
units.rightText: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

units.leftText: But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.
units.rightText: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.

units.leftText: But anyone who loves God is known by him.
units.rightText: But the one who loves God is known by God.

units.leftText: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no other God but one.
units.rightText: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

units.leftText: For though there are things that are called “gods”, whether in the heavens or on earth—as there are many “gods” and many “lords”—
units.rightText: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),

units.leftText: yet to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we live through him.
units.rightText: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

units.leftText: However, that knowledge isn’t in all men. But some, with consciousness of an idol until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
units.rightText: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

units.leftText: But food will not commend us to God. For neither, if we don’t eat are we the worse, nor if we eat are we the better.
units.rightText: But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.

units.leftText: But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
units.rightText: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.

units.leftText: For if a man sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol’s temple, won’t his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?
units.rightText: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?

units.leftText: And through your knowledge, he who is weak perishes, the brother for whose sake Christ died.
units.rightText: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.

units.leftText: Thus, sinning against the brothers, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.
units.rightText: By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will eat no meat forever more, that I don’t cause my brother to stumble.
units.rightText: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.

units.leftText: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Aren’t you my work in the Lord?
units.rightText: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?

units.leftText: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
units.rightText: Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

units.leftText: My defense to those who examine me is this:
units.rightText: This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:

units.leftText: Have we no right to eat and to drink?
units.rightText: Have we no right to food and to drink?

units.leftText: Have we no right to take along a wife who is a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
units.rightText: Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
rightNotes: 9:5 Literally take along a sister—a wife—
9:5 That is, Peter

units.leftText: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?
units.rightText: Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?
rightNotes: 9:6 Literally Or is it only Barnabas and I who do not have authority not to work?

units.leftText: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and doesn’t eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and doesn’t drink from the flock’s milk?
units.rightText: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?

units.leftText: Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or doesn’t the law also say the same thing?
units.rightText: Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?

units.leftText: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.” Is it for the oxen that God cares,
units.rightText: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
rightNotes: 9:9 Deuteronomy 25:4|DEU 25:4*

units.leftText: or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes in hope should partake of his hope.
units.rightText: Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.

units.leftText: If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?
units.rightText: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?

units.leftText: If others partake of this right over you, don’t we yet more?
units.rightText: If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.

units.leftText: Don’t you know that those who serve around sacred things eat from the things of the temple, and those who wait on the altar have their portion with the altar?
units.rightText: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?

units.leftText: Even so the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.
units.rightText: In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.

units.leftText: But I have used none of these things, and I don’t write these things that it may be done so in my case; for I would rather die, than that anyone should make my boasting void.
units.rightText: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.

units.leftText: For if I preach the Good News, I have nothing to boast about, for necessity is laid on me; but woe is to me if I don’t preach the Good News.
units.rightText: Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!

units.leftText: For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if not of my own will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.
units.rightText: If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.

units.leftText: What then is my reward? That when I preach the Good News, I may present the Good News of Christ without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Good News.
units.rightText: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.

units.leftText: For though I was free from all, I brought myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.
units.rightText: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

units.leftText: To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;
units.rightText: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.
leftNotes: 9:20 NU adds: though I myself am not under the law

units.leftText: to those who are without law, as without law (not being without law toward God, but under law toward Christ), that I might win those who are without law.
units.rightText: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.

units.leftText: To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.
units.rightText: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.

units.leftText: Now I do this for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.
units.rightText: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.

units.leftText: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, so that you may win.
units.rightText: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.

units.leftText: Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
units.rightText: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.

units.leftText: I therefore run like that, not aimlessly. I fight like that, not beating the air,
units.rightText: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.

units.leftText: but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified.
units.rightText: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.

units.leftText: Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
units.rightText: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.

units.leftText: and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
units.rightText: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.

units.leftText: and all ate the same spiritual food;
units.rightText: They all ate the same spiritual food

units.leftText: and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank of a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
units.rightText: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

units.leftText: However with most of them, God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.
units.rightText: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.

units.leftText: Don’t be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”
units.rightText: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.”
rightNotes: 10:7 Or to play; Exodus 32:6|EXO 32:6*

units.leftText: Let’s not commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.
units.rightText: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.

units.leftText: Let’s not test Christ, as some of them tested, and perished by the serpents.
units.rightText: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
rightNotes: 10:9 WH, NE, and Tischendorf test the Lord

units.leftText: Don’t grumble, as some of them also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.
units.rightText: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
rightNotes: 10:10 Literally the destroyer

units.leftText: Now all these things happened to them by way of example, and they were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.
units.rightText: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

units.leftText: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall.
units.rightText: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

units.leftText: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
units.rightText: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.

units.leftText: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
units.rightText: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

units.leftText: I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.
units.rightText: I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.

units.leftText: The cup of blessing which we bless, isn’t it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, isn’t it a sharing of the body of Christ?
units.rightText: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?

units.leftText: Because there is one loaf of bread, we, who are many, are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf of bread.
units.rightText: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.

units.leftText: Consider Israel according to the flesh. Don’t those who eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?
units.rightText: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?

units.leftText: What am I saying then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
units.rightText: Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

units.leftText: But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I don’t desire that you would have fellowship with demons.
units.rightText: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.

units.leftText: You can’t both drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You can’t both partake of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.
units.rightText: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.

units.leftText: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
units.rightText: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

units.leftText: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.
units.rightText: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.
rightNotes: 10:23 Or “All things are lawful,” twice in this verse

units.leftText: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.
units.rightText: No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.

units.leftText: Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,
units.rightText: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,

units.leftText: for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”
units.rightText: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”

units.leftText: But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.
units.rightText: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.

units.leftText: But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” don’t eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience. For “the earth is the Lord’s, with all its fullness.”
units.rightText: But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience —
rightNotes: 10:28 BYZ and TR and for the sake of conscience—for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof—

units.leftText: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other’s conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?
units.rightText: the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?

units.leftText: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced for something I give thanks for?
units.rightText: If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?

units.leftText: Whether therefore you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
units.rightText: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.

units.leftText: Give no occasion for stumbling, whether to Jews, to Greeks, or to the assembly of God;
units.rightText: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—

units.leftText: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.
units.rightText: as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.

units.leftText: Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.
units.rightText: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.

units.leftText: Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.
units.rightText: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.

units.leftText: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
units.rightText: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

units.leftText: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.
units.rightText: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.

units.leftText: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered dishonors her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaved.
units.rightText: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.

units.leftText: For if a woman is not covered, let her hair also be cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, let her be covered.
units.rightText: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.

units.leftText: For a man indeed ought not to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.
units.rightText: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

units.leftText: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;
units.rightText: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.

units.leftText: for man wasn’t created for the woman, but woman for the man.
units.rightText: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.

units.leftText: For this cause the woman ought to have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
units.rightText: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
rightNotes: 11:10 Or have authority over

units.leftText: Nevertheless, neither is the woman independent of the man, nor the man independent of the woman, in the Lord.
units.rightText: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.

units.leftText: For as woman came from man, so a man also comes through a woman; but all things are from God.
units.rightText: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.

units.leftText: Judge for yourselves. Is it appropriate that a woman pray to God unveiled?
units.rightText: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

units.leftText: Doesn’t even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
units.rightText: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,

units.leftText: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given to her for a covering.
units.rightText: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.

units.leftText: But if any man seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither do God’s assemblies.
units.rightText: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.

units.leftText: But in giving you this command I don’t praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.
units.rightText: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.

units.leftText: For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.
units.rightText: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

units.leftText: For there also must be factions among you, that those who are approved may be revealed among you.
units.rightText: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.

units.leftText: When therefore you assemble yourselves together, it is not the Lord’s supper that you eat.
units.rightText: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.

units.leftText: For in your eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.
units.rightText: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.
rightNotes: 11:21 Literally each one takes first his own meal.

units.leftText: What, don’t you have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise God’s assembly and put them to shame who don’t have enough? What shall I tell you? Shall I praise you? In this I don’t praise you.
units.rightText: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!

units.leftText: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.
units.rightText: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread,

units.leftText: When he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”
units.rightText: and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
rightNotes: 11:24 BYZ and TR which is broken for you

units.leftText: In the same way he also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”
units.rightText: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”

units.leftText: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
units.rightText: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

units.leftText: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way unworthy of the Lord will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.
units.rightText: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
rightNotes: 11:27 Or will be responsible for the

units.leftText: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup.
units.rightText: Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.

units.leftText: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy way eats and drinks judgment to himself if he doesn’t discern the Lord’s body.
units.rightText: For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
rightNotes: 11:29 BYZ and TR the body of the Lord

units.leftText: For this cause many among you are weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.
units.rightText: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.

units.leftText: For if we discerned ourselves, we wouldn’t be judged.
units.rightText: Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.

units.leftText: But when we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
units.rightText: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.

units.leftText: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
units.rightText: So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

units.leftText: But if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest your coming together be for judgment. The rest I will set in order whenever I come.
units.rightText: If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.

units.leftText: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I don’t want you to be ignorant.
units.rightText: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.

units.leftText: You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.
units.rightText: You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.

units.leftText: Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
units.rightText: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.

units.leftText: There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.
units.rightText: There are different ministries, but the same Lord.

units.leftText: There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.
units.rightText: There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.

units.leftText: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.
units.rightText: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.

units.leftText: For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
units.rightText: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

units.leftText: to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit,
units.rightText: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,

units.leftText: and to another workings of miracles, and to another prophecy, and to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of languages, and to another the interpretation of languages.
units.rightText: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

units.leftText: But the one and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.
units.rightText: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.

units.leftText: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.
units.rightText: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.

units.leftText: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.
units.rightText: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.

units.leftText: For the body is not one member, but many.
units.rightText: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.

units.leftText: If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.
units.rightText: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

units.leftText: If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.
units.rightText: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

units.leftText: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?
units.rightText: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?

units.leftText: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.
units.rightText: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.

units.leftText: If they were all one member, where would the body be?
units.rightText: If they were all one part, where would the body be?

units.leftText: But now they are many members, but one body.
units.rightText: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

units.leftText: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
units.rightText: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

units.leftText: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
units.rightText: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

units.leftText: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,
units.rightText: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,

units.leftText: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,
units.rightText: whereas our presentable parts have no such need.

units.leftText: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
units.rightText: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.

units.leftText: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
units.rightText: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.

units.leftText: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.
units.rightText: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.

units.leftText: God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.
units.rightText: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.

units.leftText: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?
units.rightText: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?

units.leftText: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?
units.rightText: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
