units.leftText: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
units.rightText: But eagerly desire the greater gifts.

units.leftText: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
units.rightText: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.

units.leftText: If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.
units.rightText: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

units.leftText: If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.
units.rightText: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
rightNotes: 13:3 SBL, NE, BYZ, and TR surrender my body to be burned

units.leftText: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
units.rightText: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

units.leftText: doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
units.rightText: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.

units.leftText: doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
units.rightText: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.

units.leftText: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
units.rightText: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

units.leftText: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.
units.rightText: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.

units.leftText: For we know in part and we prophesy in part;
units.rightText: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,

units.leftText: but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial will be done away with.
units.rightText: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.

units.leftText: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.
units.rightText: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.

units.leftText: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known.
units.rightText: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.

units.leftText: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
units.rightText: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.

units.leftText: Follow after love and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
units.rightText: Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.

units.leftText: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God, for no one understands, but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.
units.rightText: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.

units.leftText: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.
units.rightText: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.

units.leftText: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.
units.rightText: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.

units.leftText: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but even more that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.
units.rightText: I wish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. He who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified.

units.leftText: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?
units.rightText: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
leftNotes: 14:6 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Even lifeless things that make a sound, whether pipe or harp, if they didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?
units.rightText: Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?

units.leftText: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?
units.rightText: Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?

units.leftText: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.
units.rightText: So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.

units.leftText: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning.
units.rightText: Assuredly, there are many different languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.

units.leftText: If then I don’t know the meaning of the language, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.
units.rightText: If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.
rightNotes: 14:11 Literally a barbarian; twice in this verse

units.leftText: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.
units.rightText: It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.

units.leftText: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.
units.rightText: Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.

units.leftText: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.
units.rightText: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.

units.leftText: What should I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
units.rightText: What then shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.

units.leftText: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?
units.rightText: Otherwise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
rightNotes: 14:16 Or in the Spirit

units.leftText: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.
units.rightText: You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other one is not edified.

units.leftText: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.
units.rightText: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.

units.leftText: However, in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.
units.rightText: But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.

units.leftText: Brothers, don’t be children in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.
units.rightText: Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.

units.leftText: In the law it is written, “By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people. They won’t even listen to me that way, says the Lord.”
units.rightText: It is written in the Law:

units.leftText: Therefore other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to those who believe.
units.rightText: Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.

units.leftText: If therefore the whole assembly is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, won’t they say that you are crazy?
units.rightText: So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?

units.leftText: But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.
units.rightText: But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all,

units.leftText: And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.
units.rightText: and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!”

units.leftText: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, or has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.
units.rightText: What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.

units.leftText: If any man speaks in another language, let there be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.
units.rightText: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.

units.leftText: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.
units.rightText: But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God.

units.leftText: Let two or three of the prophets speak, and let the others discern.
units.rightText: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.

units.leftText: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.
units.rightText: And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.

units.leftText: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be exhorted.
units.rightText: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.

units.leftText: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,
units.rightText: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

units.leftText: for God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
units.rightText: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace— as in all the churches of the saints.
rightNotes: 14:33 Or of peace. As in all the churches of the saints: Thus, some translators begin the new paragraph after peace.

units.leftText: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,
units.rightText: Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.

units.leftText: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”
units.rightText: If they wish to inquire about something, they are to ask their own husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.
rightNotes: 14:35 Some manuscripts place verses 34–35 after verse 40.

units.leftText: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?
units.rightText: Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?

units.leftText: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.
units.rightText: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.

units.leftText: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
units.rightText: But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored.
rightNotes: 14:38 BYZ and TR let him be ignorant

units.leftText: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.
units.rightText: So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.

units.leftText: Let all things be done decently and in order.
units.rightText: But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.

units.leftText: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,
units.rightText: Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.

units.leftText: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
units.rightText: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.

units.leftText: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
units.rightText: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

units.leftText: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
units.rightText: that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

units.leftText: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
units.rightText: and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.
rightNotes: 15:5 That is, Peter

units.leftText: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.
units.rightText: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.

units.leftText: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
units.rightText: Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.

units.leftText: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.
units.rightText: And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.

units.leftText: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.
units.rightText: For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

units.leftText: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
units.rightText: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them — yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.

units.leftText: Whether then it is I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.
units.rightText: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.

units.leftText: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
units.rightText: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

units.leftText: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.
units.rightText: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.

units.leftText: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith also is in vain.
units.rightText: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.

units.leftText: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up if it is true that the dead are not raised.
units.rightText: In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.

units.leftText: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.
units.rightText: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.

units.leftText: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.
units.rightText: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.

units.leftText: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
units.rightText: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

units.leftText: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.
units.rightText: If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.

units.leftText: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep.
units.rightText: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

units.leftText: For since death came by man, the resurrection of the dead also came by man.
units.rightText: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.

units.leftText: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
units.rightText: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.

units.leftText: But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then those who are Christ’s at his coming.
units.rightText: But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.

units.leftText: Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God the Father, when he will have abolished all rule and all authority and power.
units.rightText: Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.

units.leftText: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
units.rightText: For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.

units.leftText: The last enemy that will be abolished is death.
units.rightText: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.

units.leftText: For, “He put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when he says, “All things are put in subjection”, it is evident that he is excepted who subjected all things to him.
units.rightText: For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.

units.leftText: When all things have been subjected to him, then the Son will also himself be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.
units.rightText: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.

units.leftText: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?
units.rightText: If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?

units.leftText: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?
units.rightText: And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?

units.leftText: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
units.rightText: I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
units.rightText: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised,

units.leftText: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
units.rightText: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
rightNotes: 15:33 Probably a quote from the Greek comedy Thais by Menander

units.leftText: Wake up righteously and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
units.rightText: Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.

units.leftText: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”
units.rightText: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”

units.leftText: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
units.rightText: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.

units.leftText: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.
units.rightText: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.

units.leftText: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.
units.rightText: But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.

units.leftText: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.
units.rightText: Not all flesh is the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.

units.leftText: There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.
units.rightText: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the splendor of the heavenly bodies is of one degree, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is of another.

units.leftText: There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.
units.rightText: The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.

units.leftText: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable.
units.rightText: So will it be with the resurrection of the dead: What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.

units.leftText: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
units.rightText: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

units.leftText: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is also a spiritual body.
units.rightText: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.

units.leftText: So also it is written, “The first man Adam became a living soul.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
units.rightText: So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
rightNotes: 15:45 Genesis 2:7|GEN 2:7*

units.leftText: However, that which is spiritual isn’t first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual.
units.rightText: The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.

units.leftText: The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven.
units.rightText: The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.

units.leftText: As is the one made of dust, such are those who are also made of dust; and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.
units.rightText: As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.

units.leftText: As we have borne the image of those made of dust, let’s also bear the image of the heavenly.
units.rightText: And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.
leftNotes: 15:49 NU, TR read “we will” instead of “let’s”

units.leftText: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.
units.rightText: Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
leftNotes: 15:50 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
units.rightText: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed —
leftNotes: 15:51 “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
units.rightText: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.

units.leftText: For this perishable body must become imperishable, and this mortal must put on immortality.
units.rightText: For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
rightNotes: 15:53 Or clothe itself

units.leftText: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”
units.rightText: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
rightNotes: 15:54 WH does not include and the mortal with immortality.

units.leftText: “Death, where is your sting?
units.rightText: “Where, O Death, is your victory?

units.leftText: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
units.rightText: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

units.leftText: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!

units.leftText: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
units.rightText: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

units.leftText: Now concerning the collection for the saints: as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.
units.rightText: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:

units.leftText: On the first day of every week, let each one of you save as he may prosper, that no collections are made when I come.
units.rightText: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.

units.leftText: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.
units.rightText: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me.

units.leftText: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
units.rightText: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.

units.leftText: But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.
units.rightText: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.

units.leftText: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.
units.rightText: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.

units.leftText: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,
units.rightText: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
rightNotes: 16:8 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Weeks(see Exodus 34:22|EXO 34:22*).

units.leftText: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.
units.rightText: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.

units.leftText: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.
units.rightText: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.

units.leftText: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.
units.rightText: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.

units.leftText: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.
units.rightText: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.

units.leftText: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
units.rightText: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.

units.leftText: Let all that you do be done in love.
units.rightText: Do everything in love.

units.leftText: Now I beg you, brothers—you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints—
units.rightText: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,

units.leftText: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labors.
units.rightText: to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.

units.leftText: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.
units.rightText: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.

units.leftText: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.
units.rightText: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.

units.leftText: The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in their house.
units.rightText: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings.
rightNotes: 16:19 Literally in Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey.

units.leftText: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
units.rightText: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

units.leftText: This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.
units.rightText: This greeting is in my own hand — Paul.

units.leftText: If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be cursed. Come, Lord!
units.rightText: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!
rightNotes: 16:22 Greek Marana Tha! from a transliteration of the Aramaic, an exclamation of approaching divine judgment

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
units.rightText: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

units.leftText: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
units.rightText: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus.
